title: StaticCodeAnalyser Rule Catalog
description: Single source of truth for all SCA detector rule metadata. Consumed by uRuleCatalog.pas (Delphi) and tools/gen-rules-docs.py (Markdown generator).

profiles.description: Named rule subsets. '*' expands to all kinds; additional names after '*' are additive.

id.description: Stable rule ID (SCA001..SCA999). Append-only - never recycle.

kind.description: Pascal TFindingKind name without 'fk' prefix (e.g. 'MemoryLeak'). Must match KIND_META in uSCAConsts.pas.

name.description: Short human-readable rule title shown in IDEs / dashboards.

fullDescription.description: Longer explanation - what triggers the rule, what the consequence is, how to fix.

impacts.description: SonarQube MQR impacts: software-quality dimensions this rule affects with the per-impact severity.

configKey.description: INI section/key that tunes this rule (e.g. '[Detectors] CyclomaticMax').

anchor.description: Source-place service (TSourcePlaces): what the findings of this rule anchor on. Optional; absent = the tool's compiled-in value for this rule (uRuleCatalogData.inc), 'statement' if it has none. A non-string or unknown value is ignored the same way. 'uses-item' is reserved: no rule carries it and no consumer evaluates it yet. reDelphix distinguishes only 'assign' and 'call'; every other value searches assignments and calls.

fixMode.description: Source-place service: whether a rewriting module may write on this rule's signal. Optional; absent = the tool's compiled-in value for this rule (uRuleCatalogData.inc), 'none' if it has none - so an older catalog file without this field does not switch rewriting off. A non-string or unknown value is ignored the same way. Write 'none' explicitly to switch rewriting off: then a module offers no rewriting help on this rule's signal at all (reDelphix: no Format()/SQL recipe, no line helper, no 'remove marker', no uses qualification). 'assisted' = a module may offer a template or preview but never writes into the source; 'auto' = it may write. Absent with no compiled-in value: the statement recipes (Format()/SQL) offer nothing, line-based helpers of a module decide for themselves.

editorHelp.description: Whether an IDE module offers a quick fix for this rule's findings - a code action that writes the fix in place (reDelphix: light bulb, Ctrl+Alt+F). Optional; absent = the tool's compiled-in value (uRuleCatalogData.inc), false if it has none; a non-boolean value is ignored the same way. Informational for reports (HTML 'QF' badge, 'Quick-Wins' filter): whether the quick fix applies to a given finding is decided by the module.

editorHelps.description: The quick fixes behind editorHelp, one item per menu entry (a rule can have two). Present exactly when editorHelp is true; tools/gen-quickfix-doc.py --check keeps the list identical to the IDE module's fix table and recipes. Exported per finding as SARIF result properties.editorHelp ("id:effect:slug") when the CLI runs with --sarif-editor-help (off by default). Optional; absent = the tool's compiled-in value (uRuleCatalogData.inc) if editorHelp is true, none otherwise; a malformed value is ignored the same way.

id.description: Key of the entry, positional: the rule ID for the first menu entry, '<rule ID>.2' for the second - stable while the menu entries of the rule stay the same.

effect.description: 'same' = the rewrite keeps the behaviour; 'changes' = it changes behaviour (menu entry marked, never on Ctrl+Alt+F); 'depends' = marked or not depending on the finding; 'template' = writes nothing into the source (parameterised SQL template to the clipboard).

slug.description: Short name derived from the English menu text (placeholders, '(s)' and the articles a/an/the dropped, kebab-case) - to tell the entries apart, not a stable key.

detectorUnit.description: Source file implementing the detector (e.g. 'uLeakDetector2.pas') or '(parser)' for non-detector findings.

bad.description: Anti-pattern code snippet that triggers the rule.

exceptions.description: Constructs the detector deliberately does NOT report, and why. Documents the FP gates a rule carries so users can tell 'not reported' from 'not detected'. Keep in sync with the gate comments in detectorUnit.

case.description: The construct that is exempt, phrased as the user would recognise it (e.g. 'Interface with a named ancestor').

why.description: Why reporting it would be wrong - the mechanism, not the symptom.

example.description: Optional Pascal snippet showing the exempt construct.
